notes:
I've written notes for most of Matthew 17, but a few verses are missing. My research tools stopped partway, and the two most detailed verse-by-verse sources I read (Enduring Word and Broadus) both cut off early: Enduring Word at v. 11, Broadus at v. 14. Because of that, vv. 13, 16, 18–19 and 22–23 have no notes and v. 14 has only one. I didn't find anything on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace readings of this chapter, so none are included.

---

**v. 1**
- **Traditional reading:** Clarke says Jesus took three men so there would be the two or three witnesses Scripture requires. The same three were made witnesses of his agony in the garden. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/matthew-17.html
- **Which mountain?** Guzik weighs Tabor, Hermon and Miron, and notes that Carson favours Miron. He also quotes Spurgeon, who says no one can decide. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **Against Tabor:** Broadus (Baptist) argues the old Tabor tradition is "almost certainly incorrect", partly because Tabor had a fortified city on top. Instead he places the event near Caesarea Philippi. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jbm/matthew-17.html
- **For Tabor:** The Catholic Haydock commentary says Thabor is very generally supposed to have been the mountain. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/haydock/matthew/17.htm The Orthodox Church also names Tabor by tradition. https://www.oca.org/orthodoxy/the-orthodox-faith/worship/the-church-year/transfiguration

**v. 2**
- **What "transfigured" means:** Guzik quotes Carson that the Greek word implies a change of inmost nature that can be seen outwardly. He suggests the event was not a new miracle, but the temporary cessation of an ongoing one. The real miracle was that Jesus, most of the time, could keep from displaying this glory. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-17-commentary
- **Spurgeon:** He calls it an unveiling of the Lord's hidden nature, with His face shining by its own inner glory. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-17-commentary-spurgeon
- **Matthew Henry (Presbyterian):** Christ's body stayed the same in substance and was not turned into a spirit, but it now appeared in power and glory. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/mhm/matthew-17.html
- **Broadus (Baptist):** He reads it more modestly, as merely a change in his appearance, and a preview of the glory to come. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jbm/matthew-17.html
- **Catholic:** Haydock says Christ added splendour but did not lay aside His substance. It also faults Calvin for translating the word as "transformed", calling this contrary to the Fathers. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/haydock/matthew/17.htm
- **Orthodox:** The light of Tabor was the light of the divine nature, and as such, it was Uncreated and Divine. https://www.oca.org/saints/all-lives/1000/08/06 The Orthodox recall this teaching through St Gregory Palamas, against Barlaam, who argued the light was created and material. https://www.oca.org/saints/all-lives/2020/03/15 The feast also presents Christ as showing human nature restored to its original beauty. https://www.oca.org/reflections/fr.-steven-kostoff/a-feast-of-divine-beauty

**v. 3**
- **Law and Prophets:** Moses and Elijah stand for the Law and the Prophets. Guzik also suggests a second picture: Moses for believers who die and go to glory, Elijah for those taken up without dying. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **Life after death:** Clarke says the scene confirmed belief in a future life, since Moses and Elijah were still alive centuries later. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/matthew-17.html
- **Broadus:** Luke says they talked about Jesus' "decease" (Greek *exodos*). Broadus thinks the talk partly strengthened Jesus Himself for His coming death. He calls the question of whether Moses had a resurrection body "idle". https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jbm/matthew-17.html

**v. 4**
- **Traditional reading:** Mark and Luke say Peter didn't know what he was saying. Without meaning to, his words put Jesus on a level with Moses and Elijah. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **Broadus:** He thinks Peter wanted to stay so that Jesus would not go to Jerusalem to suffer. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jbm/matthew-17.html
- **Catholic/Protestant dispute:** A Protestant source collected on Precept Austin says Catholic scholars use Moses and Elijah's appearance to support praying to the dead, and calls this a misreading. This is a Protestant description of the Catholic view; I didn't find a Catholic source making the argument. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-17-commentary
- **Shrines on the site:** Haydock records that three churches were later built on the mountain to stand for Peter's three shelters. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/haydock/matthew/17.htm

**v. 5**
- **The cloud:** It is the shekinah glory cloud. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **The words echo Scripture:** Guzik traces them to Psalm 2:7, Isaiah 42:1 and Deuteronomy 18:15. He reads the voice as correcting Peter by setting Jesus above the Law and the Prophets. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **"Listen to Him":** BibleHub's study notes link it to the promised prophet like Moses and see parallels with Sinai. https://biblehub.com/matthew/17.htm
- **Spurgeon:** He thought the voice was a greater glory than the light. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-17-commentary-spurgeon

**vv. 6–7**
- **Why they fell:** They fell down at the voice, not at the light. Guzik sees the purpose as reassuring them that Jesus was the Messiah even though He would be crucified. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **Broadus:** He compares Jesus' touch to the angel touching Daniel. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jbm/matthew-17.html

**v. 8**
- **Spurgeon:** He applies "Jesus only" devotionally: may Christ fill our whole view. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-17-commentary-spurgeon
- **Broadus disagrees:** He says the phrase only means the others were gone. Using it as a text for "trust Jesus only" is does not always imply saving faith. For him it is a special, God-given certainty for a particular miracle at that moment. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-20.html
  - Spurgeon (Baptist) applies it broadly: the church needs more faith, and even mountains of sin must move if faith is strong. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-20.html
- **Catholic:** Haydock cites Jerome that "mountains" means the hardest tasks. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/haydock/matthew/17.htm

**v. 21**
- **Not in the oldest manuscripts:** The NET note says this verse is almost certainly not original. It was probably copied in from Mark 9:29. https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Mat&chapter=17&verse=21
- **Older commentators agree:** Clarke suspected the verse was added, though very early. Spurgeon accepted that it was added and said it makes no real difference, since Mark has the saying. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-21.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** It takes the verse as hinting at ranks among demons. https://biblehub.com/matthew/17-21.htm
- **Catholic:** Haydock uses the verse to defend fasting against those who ridicule it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/haydock/matthew/17.htm

**v. 24**
- **What tax?** It was not a Roman tax but the half-shekel for the temple (Exodus 30:13). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-24.html
- **Was it voluntary?** Gill and others thought the payment was voluntary but expected. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/17-24.htm

**vv. 25–26**
- **Main reading:** As Son of the God whose house the temple is, Jesus owes nothing (Benson, Barnes). https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-27.html
- **Real difference: are the disciples "sons" too?**
  - MacLaren says the plural "sons" does not put Peter in the same class as Jesus. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/maclaren_alexander/expositions-of-holy-scripture/matthew/the-coin-in-the-fishs-mouth.cfm
  - Ligonier (Reformed) says Jesus and His followers are exempt as children of God, because Christ is greater than the temple. https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/jesus-provides-shekel
  - Piper (Baptist) agrees, and says the temple is passing away. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-sons-are-free

**v. 27**
- **Why pay?** To avoid needless offence. Guzik sees a picture of redemption: Jesus pays a debt He doesn't owe and covers us too. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-17/
- **Henry's atonement point:** The tax was called "an atonement for the soul", and Christ paid it though He had no sin to atone for. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-24.html
- **Henry against Catholic claims:** He rejects the idea that paying for Peter made Peter head of the church. To him, it was a sign of Peter being under authority, not above others. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-24.html
- **Applied to giving:** Piper applies the passage to the freedom Christians have in deciding whether to fund church buildings. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-sons-are-free
- **Sceptical readings:**
  - Peake's Commentary notes the text never says Peter found the coin, and calls it a "half-made" miracle story. It also mentions J. Weiss's view that the real issue was later Christians paying the same tax to Rome. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/pfc/matthew-17.html
  - Barclay argues that taken literally the miracle would even be immoral. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/17-27.html
